title: Monitoring endothelial cell development and migration in the embryonic CNS
protocol: Collect mouse embryos one by one from deeply anesthetized dams.
Decapitate each embryo immediately upon removal and remove the brains.
Immerse the brains in 4% paraformaldehyde in 0.1M phosphate buffer, pH 7.2.
Store the fixed brains at 4°C.
Wash the brains three times in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Permeabilize the brains with 1% bovine serum albumen (BSA) and 0.5% TritonX-100 in PBS at 4°C overnight.
Rinse the brains in PBS for 5 minutes.
Incubate the brains in biotinylated isolectin B4 (1:40) in antibody diluent solution containing 1% TritonX-100 at 4°C overnight.
Wash the brains six times in PBS, each wash lasting 4 minutes.
Incubate the brains with Alexa 594 streptavidin conjugate diluted 1:200 in antibody diluent containing 0.5% TritonX-100 for 6 hours at 4°C.
Rinse the brains six times in PBS, each rinse lasting 4 minutes.
Place the brains in a 35 mm Petri dish containing PBS and view under a dissecting microscope.
Separate the telencephalon from the rest of the brain by severing the nascent internal capsule as close to the ganglionic eminences as possible using spring scissors.
Separate the telencephalic hemispheres from each other by making a mid-line cut with a scalpel blade (number 11).
Cut each hemisphere along the caudal to rostral direction and open like a book to reveal the ganglionic eminences at the base of the telencephalon.
Mount the open hemisphere flat with the ventricular surface facing the viewer on Superfrost Plus glass slides.
Apply Vectashield hard setTM mounting medium to the slides.
Examine the mounted hemispheres using a Zeiss Pascal LSM 5 laser confocal microscope.
Under a microscope, cut the telencephalon along the caudal to rostral direction with fine microtip scissors.
Trim the floor plate gently to flatten the tissue.
Separate the dorsal and ventral telencephalon by making an incision at the dorso-ventral boundary.
Transfer each telencephalic explant to polycarbonate membranes (8 mm pore size) in sterile 6 well plates containing NeurobasalTM medium.
Place the plates in the incubator (37°C, 5% CO2 and 95% humidity).
Test cell viability in the explants with a LIVE/DEAD® Viability/Cytotoxicity Kit.
Incubate the explant with Qtracker reagents (Qtracker 655 Cell Labeling Kit) in NeurobasalTM medium for 45 min at 37°C.
Transfer the dorsal explant to the polycarbonate membrane.
Graft the labeled ventral explant onto the unlabeled dorsal explant using fine tungsten needles.
Visualize the labeled explant with a fluorescence microscope to confirm appropriate positioning.
Incubate the explants for 24 h at 37°C (5% CO2 and 95% humidity) in NeurobasalTM medium.
Detach the explants from the membrane filters gently into petri dishes.
Fix the explants in zinc fixative at room temperature for 24 hours.
Transfer the fixed explants into a glass vial.
Dehydrate the explants in 70% ethanol for 1 hour.
Dehydrate the explants in 95% ethanol for 1 hour.
Dehydrate the explants twice in 100% ethanol for 1 hour each.
Clear the explants in xylene for 1 hour.
Place the vial containing the explants to 25% capacity with fresh xylene and transfer to a 60°C oven.
After 15 minutes, add molten paraffin wax to the vial so that the ratio of wax to xylene is 1:1.
After 30 minutes, increase the ratio of wax to xylene to 2:1 by adding more paraffin.
Replace the paraffin-xylene mixture with fresh paraffin after an additional 30 minutes.
Immerse the explants overnight in fresh paraffin at 60°C.
Embed the explants flat in paraffin in a plastic mold and leave at room temperature for 24 hours.
Remove the paraffin block containing the explant from the mold, trim it, and section on a rotary microtome in the coronal plane at 15 μm thickness.
Mount the sections on Superfrost Plus glass slides.
Dry the mounted sections at 37°C for 24 hours.
Deparaffinize the sections in xylene (two changes, 10 minutes each).
Rehydrate the sections in descending series of ethanol (100%, 95%, 70%), each for 10 minutes.
Transfer the rehydrated sections to PBS.
Treat the sections with BD Retrievagen (pH 6.0) before immunohistochemical staining.
Stain the sections using standard methods for immunohistochemistry.
Transplant mouse brain-derived endothelial cells treated with siRNA into E11 wild type CD1 ventral telencephalon explants.
Study the migratory behavior of transplanted endothelial cells.
Use embryonic mouse endothelial cells prepared from Nkx2.1-/- and SeyDey mice in parallel studies.
Collect E13 embryos for primary endothelial cell cultures.
Dissect the telencephalon and separate into ventral and dorsal compartments by an incision at the dorso-ventral boundary.
Mince tissue pieces into 1-2 mm fragments with a scalpel blade.
Rinse minced tissue in PBS.
Incubate tissue fragments at 37°C for 0.5 h in pre-warmed PBS containing trypsin (0.25%), DNase I (1 mg/ml), and EDTA (0.5 mM).
Dissociate the tissue, spin it down, re-suspend in warm 10% fetal calf serum (FCS)-DMEM.
Filter through a sterile 40 μm nylon mesh to collect cells.
Resuspend cell pellet in 1 ml RBC lysing buffer (Sigma).
Overlay onto DMEM and centrifuge briefly.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 ml of 10% FCS-DMEM.
Coat dynabeads with sheep anti-rat IgG (Invitrogen) at 4°C overnight.
Incubate coated beads with rat anti-mouse CD31 (PECAM-1) monoclonal antibody (BD Pharmingen) at 4°C overnight and wash three times with 2% FCS in PBS.
Add 1 ml of cell suspension to the tube containing washed beads.
Incubate mixture for 30 min at 4°C with occasional agitation.
Recover bead-bound cells using a magnetic field, wash five times in 10% FCS-DMEM and once with FCS-free DMEM.
Digest bead-free cells for 10 min at 37°C in 1 ml of trypsin/EDTA (GIBCO) to release the beads.
Centrifuge bead-free cells in 10% FCS-DMEM.
Resuspend cells in endothelial cell culture medium (BIOCOAT Endothelial Cell Growth Environment, BD Biosciences).
Culture cells in 75 cm² BIOCOAT® Collagen Type I flasks (BD Biosciences).
Feed the cells every 2 days with complete medium exchange.
Trypsinize cells for subculture when they reach 80% confluency.
Split cells into 6 well plates.
Maintain cells in DMEM before transfection with siRNA constructs.
Use pre-designed siRNA constructs for Nkx2.1 and a control non-targeting siRNA from Dharmacon.
Co-transfect endothelial cells at 80% confluency in DMEM with siGLO Red transfection indicator using DharmaFECT reagent 1.
Transfect with 2 μM of siRNA and 1 μM of siGLO Red transfection indicator.
Observe virtually complete knockdown of NKX2.1 within 96 hours by western blotting and immunocytochemistry.
Spin down cells before transplantation.
Collect the cells in 200 μl DMEM.
Prepare explants of E11 mouse CD1 telencephalon on polycarbonate membrane in sterile 6 well plates in DMEM.
Ensure the upper surface of the explant is exposed to air for transplantation.
Take approximately 100 endothelial cells in a fine micropipette.
Pressure inject the cells focally into the explant.
Leave the plates untouched for 15-20 minutes.
Transfer the plates into the incubator.
One hour after transplantation, add more medium to fully submerge the explants.
Process the explants for paraffin wax histology and immunohistochemistry after 24 hours.
